message.content:
The quadratic equation is  

\[
x^{2}+2x+3=0
\]

Using the quadratic formula \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}\):

* Discriminant: \(b^{2}-4ac = 2^{2}-4(1)(3)=4-12=-8\).

Since the discriminant is negative, the roots are complex:

\[
x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{-8}}{2}
   =\frac{-2\pm 2i\sqrt{2}}{2}
   =-1 \pm i\sqrt{2}.
\]

So the two solutions are  

\[
\boxed{x = -1 + i\sqrt{2}}\quad\text{and}\quad\boxed{x = -1 - i\sqrt{2}}.
\]

So complex roots: (-b ± sqrt(discriminant)) / (2a) = (-2 ± sqrt(-8)) / 2 = (-2 ± 2i*sqrt(2)) / 2 = -1 ± i*sqrt(2). So solutions: x = -1 + i√2, x = -1 - i√2.
